intended_object: The vector R(πt)·p in ℝ³, where R(θ) is rotation by θ about the z-axis (in the first two coordinates), applied to a point p of the equator of S² for t ∈ [0,1]. It is the underlying function of the half-turn homotopy from the identity to the antipodal map on the equator. Inferred from the docstring and the later definition sphere2EquatorHalfTurnMap.
explanation: The body computes (cos(πt)x − sin(πt)y, sin(πt)x + cos(πt)y, 0). That is exactly the rotation of (x, y) by angle πt with the third coordinate set to zero, as the docstring describes. Equator points have z = 0, so this equals the full z-axis rotation of p. It gives p at t = 0 and −p at t = 1, and the library proves it has norm 1, so it stays on the sphere. It is a specific concrete map whose content needs this particular setting (the equator of S² in ℝ³), so it is not too narrow.
